headline: Argentine Sovereign Risk Rises Amid Global Market Sell-Off
summary: Argentine sovereign bonds declined by an average of 1.1% while the JP Morgan country risk index rose to 852 points following Wall Street's tech sell-off.
why: Emerging market sovereign debt yields and risk spreads are sensitive to external financial conditions and global risk appetite.

impacts.name: Argentina
impacts.why: Rising sovereign risk spreads reflect increased borrowing costs and declining bond prices for the country.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: A global equity sell-off and rising risk aversion in international markets spilled over into emerging market debt, pushing Argentine bond prices lower and increasing the country risk index.
